concept.title: What is a Treap?
concept.description: A Treap is a combination of a Binary Search Tree (BST) and a Heap. Each node has a key (follows BST ordering: left < parent < right) and a random priority (follows max-heap ordering: parent priority >= child priority). Rotations maintain the heap property after insertions.
concept.analogy: Like a tournament bracket where seeded players (priorities) determine placement, but match order follows alphabetical (BST) rules!

complexity.title: Time Complexity
complexity.note: Random priorities give O(log n) expected height, making worst-case O(n) extremely unlikely.

useCases.title: Common Use Cases
items: Implicit key treaps for sequence operations
Randomized balanced BST without complex rebalancing

items.advantage: Expected O(log n) balance via random priorities
